issue_context.title: Fix null reference exception, support encoding in Compression.UnzipData
issue_context.body:
These two commits are pulled out of #1040 as they're a quick and easy review and should be merged regardless of that issue's final result.

#### Expected Behavior
<!--- Required. Describe the behavior you expect to see for your case. -->
* Null reference exceptions shouldn't be thrown when checking `result.Success`. This was happening when receiving an empty string as a response.
* Support specifying an `Encoding` in `Compression.UnzipData` which calls int `string.GetBytes(Encoding)`. This issue here was the `GetBytes` function defaults to `Encoding.ASCII` which is _almost_ never a good idea, unless you're absolutely positive the character set will be restricted to 7 bits.

#### Actual Behavior
<!--- Required. Describe the actual behavior for your case. -->
Null refs abound and `GetBytes` assumes single byte characters, failed on unicode characters, which are valid keys of a dictionar (string is C# are UTF16, double wide)

#### Potential Solution
<!--- Optional. Describe any potential solutions and/or thoughts as to what may be causing the difference between expected and actual behavior. -->
Check response for null and allow specifying `Encoding`

#### Reproducing the Problem
<!--- Required for Bugs. Describe how to reproduce the problem. This can be via a failing unit test or a simplified algorithm that reliably demonstrates this issue.  -->
Visual inspection.

review_comments: I'm not sure if we want this here, but it was pretty useful for debugging. How often are we expecting unsuccessful messages, and is there any reason we _shouldn't_ log those responses?

This error condition shouldn't be too frequent since exceptions should already be caught on L107,
agree with logging the error here.

Nice catch! 
I was seeing quite a few null refs on these API calls in syslogs 👍
